<PubmedArticle><MedlineCitation Status="MEDLINE" Owner="NLM" IndexingMethod="Manual"><PMID Version="1">28609014</PMID><DateCompleted><Year>2019</Year><Month>07</Month><Day>24</Day></DateCompleted><DateRevised><Year>2019</Year><Month>07</Month><Day>24</Day></DateRevised><Article PubModel="Print-Electronic"><Journal><ISSN IssnType="Electronic">1098-1063</ISSN><JournalIssue CitedMedium="Internet"><Volume>28</Volume><Issue>9</Issue><PubDate><Year>2018</Year><Month>Sep</Month></PubDate></JournalIssue><Title>Hippocampus</Title><ISOAbbreviation>Hippocampus</ISOAbbreviation></Journal><ArticleTitle>Space, time, and episodic memory: The hippocampus is all over the cognitive map.</ArticleTitle><Pagination><StartPage>680</StartPage><EndPage>687</EndPage><MedlinePgn>680-687</MedlinePgn></Pagination><ELocationID EIdType="doi" ValidYN="Y">10.1002/hipo.22750</ELocationID><Abstract><AbstractText>In recent years, the field has reached an impasse between models suggesting that the hippocampus is fundamentally involved in spatial processing and models suggesting that the hippocampus automatically encodes all dimensions of experience in the service of memory. Here, we consider key conceptual issues that have impeded progress in our understanding of hippocampal function, and we review findings that establish the scope and limits of hippocampal involvement in navigation and memory. We argue that space and time serve as a primary scaffold to break up experiences into specific contexts, and to organize multimodal input that is to be associated within a context. However, the hippocampus is clearly capable of incorporating additional dimensions into the scaffold if they are determined to be relevant in the event-defined context. Conceiving of the hippocampal representation as constrained by immediate task demands-yet preferring axes that involve space and time-helps to reconcile an otherwise disparate set of findings on the core function of the hippocampus.</AbstractText><CopyrightInformation>&#xa9; 2018 Wiley Periodicals, Inc.</CopyrightInformation></Abstract><AuthorList CompleteYN="Y"><Author
